messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager alert — inference-prod high tail latency (p95 > 1.2s) — detected by latency-checker. alert_id=ALRT-7753. Paging on-call primary.

maya (oncall-primary): I’m on it. seeing increased p95 on /v1/generate, looks correlated with model-worker CPU spikes. grabbing logs.

devon (oncall-secondary): I’m here as backup. if primary needs escalation, page infra.

maya (oncall-primary): checked prometheus: node gpu-utilization at 95% on gpu-pool-3. KV cache hitrate dropped ~30%. curious if a bad rollout hit a larger model.

sam (sre): @maya can you paste the last 2m of logs from inference-api? run: 

```
kubectl -n inference-prod logs deploy/inference-api --tail=200 | sed -n '1,200p'
```

maya (oncall-primary): paste below snippet from the API: 

```
2026-05-11T18:12:01Z INFO request id=abc123 model=redwood-large seq_len=1024 tokens=12 time_ms=278
2026-05-11T18:12:05Z WARN request id=def456 model=redwood-hybrid seq_len=2048 tokens=16 time_ms=1042
2026-05-11T18:12:07Z ERROR kvcache miss key=conv-usr-879 status=miss
```

maya (oncall-primary): multiple requests spiking on redwood-hybrid. can someone check recent deploys?

deploy-bot: new rollout (redwood-hybrid:v3.2.1) finished at 2026-05-11T17:55:10Z, 40% traffic.

maya (oncall-primary): okay that matches. rolling back or routing away would help. devon can we divert 100% traffic to redwood-small for now?

devon (oncall-secondary): I can flip routing. executing route change now — will update after DNS/feature flag flips.

devon (oncall-secondary): flipped flag in feature-gates: 

```
POST /api/feature-gates/route
{ "model":"redwood-small", "percent":100 }
```

maya (oncall-primary): traffic diverted. p95 dropping to 230ms within 60s. nice.

alin (infra-lead): good mitigation. we should still investigate why v3.2.1 causes high memory/KV churn. @sam can you grab heap profiles from the worker pods and open infra ticket?

sam (sre): will collect profiles now. also creating a bug with perf traces: BUG-1429. tagging @research for model regression.

kate (product-support): FYI I notified the biggest affected customer cohort (enterprise accounts with >1k qps) about temporary mitigation and potential degraded quality during reroute.

maya (oncall-primary): temporary runbook checklist used: 
1) identify offending model/deploy
2) divert traffic via feature-gate or traffic-router
3) if divert unavailable, scale up dedicated pool or enable burst capacity
4) page infra if KV/cache subsystem shows >20% miss increase for >5m

maya (oncall-primary): quick note on escalation policy we used: 
- page on-call primary (this thread) on any SLO >5% breach or customer-impacting error rate >1%
- if primary cannot mitigate within 10m, escalate to on-call-secondary and infra-lead (@alin)
- if mitigation involves infra changes (scaling, kernel-level flags), page infra pager and infra-lead immediately
- for multi-region failover >15m, page oncall-manager and create incident bridge

devon (oncall-secondary): adding some handoff notes — my upcoming shift starts in 20m; maya if you still have this open at handoff, call it out in the warm-handoff and note: diverted to redwood-small, rollback of redwood-hybrid pending investigation, BUG-1429 open, postmortem owner=maya.

maya (oncall-primary): noted. I’ll do a warm-handoff message 5m before shift end with current state and next steps.

alin (infra-lead): escalation recipients in order: infra-pager -> network-pager -> db-pager. page infra immediately if kernel OOMs or node-level contention observed. For paging content, include alert_id, affected routes, mitigation steps taken, and whether rollback attempted.

sam (sre): attaching quick triage commands used: 
```
# check kvcache hitrate
promql: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits[1m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests[1m]))
# pod mem + cpu
kubectl top pods -n inference-prod
```

maya (oncall-primary): summary for runbook: /runbooks/inference/high-latency.md — added a step to check recent model rollouts and feature-gate routing.

devon (oncall-secondary): small coverage gap note: between 19:00-19:30 UTC there’s only one engineer signed up (me) due to shift swap. If heavy work queued, page oncall-manager for extra eyes.

maya (oncall-primary): resolved: p95 back to normal for 5 consecutive minutes, closing the alert. mitigation: traffic routed to redwood-small, rollback withheld pending perf investigation.

IncidentBot: Alert ALRT-7753 status=resolved. duration=8m41s. incident_id=INC-2026-05311-1.

maya (oncall-primary): follow-up actions: 1) infra to collect heap/profile traces (sam) 2) model team to run regression tests on v3.2.1 (research) 3) postmortem draft by Friday — I’ll own.

kate (product-support): thanks all — I’ll follow up with impacted customers and link PM notes to the postmortem.

devon (oncall-secondary): warm-handoff note posted to #eng-oncall: next oncall is devon at 19:00 UTC, secondary will be alin.

maya (oncall-primary): handing off: status=stable, mitigation=traffic-reroute, next-steps=investigate KV churn, postmortem owner=maya. signing off. :white_check_mark:
